summary: Master has not made this moot, since verify still passes cu_seqlens_q. The mechanism doesn't hold up, though: cache_seqlens (seqused_k) already puts FA3 on its Varlen instantiation with the varlen tile scheduler and prepare_varlen_num_blocks, and page-size-1 paged KV forces PackGQA with cp.async Q loads. Dropping cu_seqlens_q only swaps a few runtime offset reads inside the same kernel binary, so the expected effect is well under the ~1.5% per-shape drift and one run cannot resolve it.
justification: Not moot: master's kernel_fn still calls flash_attn_with_kvcache with cu_seqlens_q=data['cu_seqlens_q'] and max_seqlen_q=length on every shape, including the paired full-layer path at batch > 1 (q is [tokens, Hq, 128], heads=1, metadata=None) and the unpaired path elsewhere. The mechanism is where it fails. (1) Upstream FA3 hopper picks its Varlen template when any of cu_seqlens_q, cu_seqlens_k, seqused_q, seqused_k or leftpad_k is set. cache_seqlens is seqused_k, so the batched form still runs Varlen=true: the same varlen tile scheduler and the same prepare_varlen_num_blocks_kernel. FINDINGS shows that kernel on every shape, decode q_len 1 included (1.8-3.4 us). There is no 'static batched scheduler' to switch to. (2) FA3 forces pack_gqa whenever page_table is set and paged KV is not TMA-able, and page_size 1 is the non-TMA case. Q is then loaded by the PackGQA cp.async path in both forms, so the 'TMA Q load' gain does not exist. (3) Only is_varlen_q changes at runtime: a cu_seqlens_q load and an offset per tile, against 7.7-18 us of FA3 main kernel plus 2.5-12 us combine on the batch-1 verify shapes. The expected sliding verify_1/16/32 and full verify_1 'faster' rows are therefore well under 1% of shape time. The judge's drift is 1.5-2.5% per shape (LESSONS), so a gain or a loss would both be noise. The flat expectations for full verify_16/32 and decode are fine. Weakest link: the claim that the batched 4-D q takes a different FA3 code path (TMA Q plus a non-varlen scheduler). With seqused_k and page-size-1 paging it does not. The one residual unknown is whether the sgl_kernel FA3 fork departs from upstream here; a profile showing the same kernel names (prepare_varlen_num_blocks present, same flash fwd template) would confirm it.
confounders: fa3-hdim128-head-pairing / paired-heads-launch-cleanup: at batch 16/32 on full layers q is the padded [tokens, Hq, 128] tensor with Hkv'=1 super-head. The batched view must be q.view(B, 8, Hq, 2*D), not (B, 8, Hq, 64) as the spec says. The output is then [B, 8, Hq, 128] and must reach _paired_norm_gate_kernel as view(tokens, Hq, 2D) with the same strides. This is a correctness trap in the spec, not a measurement confounder.

paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate: the full verify_1 shape the spec expects to speed up is now the unpaired path (batch 1 is gated out), and the full verify_16/32 shapes are the paired path. The two paths have different qhead_per_khead (8 vs 16) but both force pack_gqa, so the gate does not change the conclusion.
fused-preattention-triton: it writes q contiguous as [tokens, Hq, D or 2D], so the 4-D view is free. It does not interact with the change.
interference: No companion would help. Both the change and the landed paths run the same FA3 instantiation, and the predicted effect is below what one run can resolve. An ab-revert of the pairing or the batch gate would only change which q shape is viewed, not whether FA3 leaves its varlen path, and a control cannot isolate a sub-change of a one-argument edit. The cheap way to settle it is offline: read sgl_kernel's flash_api.cpp, or inspect the kernel names in an existing profile. If the fork matches upstream (Varlen switch includes seqused_k; pack_gqa is forced for non-TMA paged KV), the hypothesis is inert. If the fork really does dispatch a non-varlen kernel when cu_seqlens_q is None, it can be unheld and run as written, with the paired q view fixed.
rules_flags: None. cu_seqlens_q goes unused (dropping an input is allowed), the branch is on config q_len only, and there are no host syncs, no caching, no precision change and no key skipping.

Implementation trap, not a rule: on the paired path the view must be (B, 8, Hq, 128). Using (B, 8, Hq, 64) silently halves the head dim and fails correctness on the full q_len-8 tests (batch 2 ctx 100000, batch 4 ctx 6000 edges, dp ctx 20000).
open_questions: Does the sgl_kernel FA3 fork's run_mha_fwd still include seqused_k in its VARLEN_SWITCH, and does get_pack_gqa still force packing when page_table is set without pagedkv_tma? If both hold, this hypothesis and its sibling fa3-drop-cu-seqlens-decode share the same false premise and both should be held.

If FA3 does take a non-varlen path without cu_seqlens_q, does it still launch prepare_varlen_num_blocks? Removing that 1.8-3.2 us launch would be the only effect worth measuring, and it would show in top_kernels.
